comparisons.peer_summary: Net credit losses increased 40% to $9.0 billion, with consumer net credit losses rising 39% to $8.6 billion and corporate net credit losses increasing to $397 million from $250 million.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures report on the deterioration of credit quality and increase in losses for 2024, though they focus on different segments. Bank of America reports a specific increase of $555 million in nonperforming commercial loans, primarily in the U.S. commercial segment. In contrast, Citigroup reports a broader increase in net credit losses of $9.0 billion (up 40%), where corporate (commercial) net credit losses increased to $397 million from $250 million, alongside a massive rise in consumer net credit losses. While BAC highlights the nonperforming status of commercial loans, C highlights the net credit loss amounts across both corporate and consumer lines.
